newsitem.title: UK: Eurotunnel Commission to convene at 1300 GMT.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel Commission to convene at 1300 GMT.

text.p: The Anglo-French Intergovernmental Commission, which governs Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel SA /Plc, is due to meet in Paris at 1300 GMT on Thursday, a spokeswoman for Britain's Department of Transport said.
The IGC is due to decide whether or not to allow Eurotunnel to reopen its freight shuttle service for trucks, which has been closed due to safety concerns ever since the blaze in November last year.
The IGC had been expected to make its decision last week following the recommendations of the Channel Tunnel Safety Authority (CTSA).
But Britain's new deputy prime minister and head of the transport and environment John Prescott wanted more time to review the CTSA report and concerns over the safety of the Shuttle freight wagons.
The open-lattice design of the wagons was blamed by fire chiefs for fanning the flames of the blaze on Novemeber 18 last year and allowing it to spread.
But Eurotunnel has resisted a change in design, not least because it is struggling to get out from under a mountain of debt, currently totalling some nine billion pounds.
It also argues that enclosing the wagons to reduce the fire risk would make them too high for the tunnel and break weight restrictions for track safety.
